One month.
High in the mountains, a small village sits beside a lake, lit only by its own windows.
Every pine on these slopes would be dying.
Without light, no plant can make food.
And without plants, every food chain on Earth would start to collapse.
The lake has been losing its heat for a month.
Now the ice is reaching out from the shore.
Ice floats, because water expands when it freezes.
So the lake would freeze from the top down, like a lid.
Underneath, the water would stay liquid for a long time.
Six months.
The air would be too cold to hold any water.
The clouds would fade, and the snow would stop.
In the houses, people would burn whatever they could find to stay warm.
The square would stay empty.
One year.
Minus seventy-three degrees.
With no Sun and no Moon, the Milky Way would stretch from peak to peak.
Every bit of light left on this mountain would come from the people who still live here.
And the Sun would never rise again.
